catalog_quote: First, Kagoshima Japanese permits only two accentual (or tonal) patterns, traditionally called A and B (Hirayama 1951). Tone A involves a pitch fall towards the end of the word, with only the penultimate syllable high-toned. Tone B, on the other hand, does not involve an abrupt pitch fall and keeps only the final syllable high- toned. ... (1) ka.NA.da 'Canada', DOI.tu 'Germany', IN.do 'India', HA.wai 'Hawaii', su.WEE.den 'Sweden' (2) a.me.ri.KA 'America', i.gi.ri.SU 'England, Britain', hu.ran.SU 'France' ... A second salient feature of Kagoshima Japanese is that its prosodic system is based on the syllable rather than the mora ... The loci of high tone in (1), for example, can be generalized by stating 'find the second syllable from the end of the word and keep it high-toned.' ... sources.quote: 'KJ is often referred to as a two-pattern type dialect ... These two accentual patterns are realised as [L(n)HL] and [L(n)H] where n = positive integers or zero. The former is referred to as Type A and the latter as Type B.' p.48-49: 'In the words in the left column of Table 2.3, only the penultimate syllable of a word has a high pitch ... In the words in the right column, only the last syllable of a word has a high pitch'; Hirayama's (1957, 1960) terms Type A/Type B adopted; Type A/B split 51%/49% in a 20-page sample of Hirayama 1960; p.50: 'if a particle such as -ga ... is attached to a word
